name: Retrieval Benchmark V2
description: Hard retrieval benchmark with near-duplicate policies, semantic paraphrases, scope/tier conflicts, numeric inference, and multi-source questions.

documents.text:
Atlas Cloud Security Standard — Audit Evidence (2026)
This standard governs production Enterprise workspaces. Security event records are preserved for 400 days in the managed audit store. 
Workspace administrators may continuously export the same events to an external SIEM. Authentication, API-key lifecycle, role changes,
connector administration, and destructive document actions are included. The 400-day period is the default for production Enterprise tenants.
A shorter value from the retired 2024 handbook must not be used for new contracts. Customer-generated application logs are outside this policy.

Atlas Cloud Security Handbook — Archived 2024 Edition
This archived handbook described the former audit-log program. Enterprise event history was kept for 180 days in the managed service.
The document remains available only for historical comparison and migration reviews. It is superseded by the 2026 Security Standard.
References to 180-day retention should not be applied to newly provisioned production workspaces.

Atlas Production Incident Response Standard
A Priority Zero production outage receives human acknowledgement within 12 minutes, any time of day. Priority One incidents have a 45-minute
acknowledgement target. The on-call team operates continuously, including weekends and public holidays. These targets apply to production
Enterprise and Business plans. Restoration time is not guaranteed by the acknowledgement target.

Atlas Sandbox Support Guide
Sandbox and developer-preview environments are handled during weekday support hours. A critical sandbox interruption is normally acknowledged
within 4 business hours. Sandbox incidents do not use the production Priority Zero 12-minute target. This guide is for non-production testing only.

Atlas Enterprise Resilience Plan
Production Enterprise databases use continuous replication plus scheduled snapshots. The recovery point objective is 10 minutes, meaning the design
aims to limit data loss to no more than ten minutes. The recovery time objective for a regional database failure is 90 minutes. Quarterly exercises
validate restore procedures. These objectives apply to the managed production database tier.

Atlas Analytics Warehouse Recovery Notes
The internal analytics warehouse is restored from nightly snapshots. Its recovery point objective is 24 hours and its recovery time objective is 8 hours.
These figures concern reporting and business-intelligence workloads, not the customer-facing production database service.

Atlas API Capacity — Enterprise
Enterprise API keys may sustain 1,200 requests per minute per workspace. Short bursts can reach 300 requests in a ten-second window.
When a limit is exceeded, clients receive HTTP 429 and should apply exponential backoff. Capacity increases above the documented ceiling
require an approved quota request. Limits are counted separately for each workspace.

Atlas API Capacity — Starter
Starter workspaces are limited to 120 requests per minute. Burst traffic is capped at 40 requests per ten seconds. HTTP 429 indicates throttling.
Starter quotas are intentionally lower than Enterprise quotas and are not automatically raised when usage grows.

Atlas EU Data Residency Addendum
Customers selecting the EU-resident deployment store primary customer content in Frankfurt and replicated backups in Dublin. Routine processing stays
inside the European Economic Area. Support personnel outside the EEA may access a tenant only through an approved, logged support procedure when the
customer has enabled such support access. This addendum applies only to EU-resident deployments.

Atlas Global Deployment Guide
The standard global deployment stores primary customer content in Virginia and replicated backups in Oregon. It is designed for customers who have not
selected a regional residency addendum. The global guide does not describe EU-resident storage locations.

Atlas Customer-Managed Encryption Keys
Tenants using customer-managed keys must rotate the wrapping key at least once every 120 days. Atlas accepts overlap between old and new key versions
for a 48-hour migration period. Disabling the previous version before migration completes can make stored objects temporarily unreadable.

Atlas Platform-Managed Encryption
For the default platform-managed encryption service, Atlas rotates internal wrapping material every 30 days without customer action. Customers do not
upload or schedule these platform keys. The 30-day internal cadence is distinct from the 120-day customer-managed requirement.

Atlas Enterprise Identity Administration
Enterprise tenants can enforce SAML single sign-on and automate user lifecycle management through SCIM. When SCIM is enabled, deprovisioning a user
in the identity provider disables Atlas access within 15 minutes under normal operation. Just-in-time SAML creation may be disabled when SCIM is the
authoritative provisioning source.

Atlas Team Plan Identity Guide
Team workspaces support SAML login but do not include SCIM lifecycle provisioning. User removal is performed manually by a workspace administrator.
The Team plan therefore has no fifteen-minute automated deprovisioning objective.

Atlas Customer Content Deletion Standard
When a workspace administrator permanently deletes a source document, the active copy and derived retrieval chunks are queued for irreversible removal
within 21 days. Search indexes are invalidated immediately so deleted content is no longer returned to users. Disaster-recovery backups age out on their
normal rolling schedule and are not individually edited.

Atlas Account Closure Procedure
Closing an entire customer account begins a separate offboarding process. Billing records required for statutory accounting may be retained for seven years,
while operational tenant data is scheduled for deletion after the contractual closure window. This procedure is not the document-level deletion standard.

Atlas Enterprise Support Coverage
Enterprise customers receive staffed technical support 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Standard non-incident requests have a two-hour first-response
objective. Named technical account reviews occur monthly. This support coverage is separate from incident severity acknowledgement targets.

Atlas Business Support Coverage
Business customers receive staffed technical support from 08:00 to 20:00 local business time, Monday through Friday. Standard requests have an eight-hour
first-response objective measured during covered hours. Weekend coverage is not included unless separately purchased.

Atlas Google Drive Connector
After initial indexing, the Google Drive connector checks for changed files every 5 minutes. Permission changes are synchronized during the same polling
cycle. Administrators can also request a manual refresh. Very large drives may require additional processing time after a change is discovered.

Atlas SharePoint Connector
The SharePoint connector polls for changed documents every 30 minutes after initial indexing. Access-control changes are processed with the content delta.
A manual synchronization can be initiated by an administrator. The thirty-minute cadence is specific to SharePoint.

Atlas High-Risk Model Governance
A model classified as high risk cannot be promoted to production until it passes red-team review, privacy review, and an offline quality gate of at least
92 percent on the approved task benchmark. Any material prompt, retrieval, or fine-tuning change requires reevaluation before the next production release.

Atlas Standard Model Governance
Standard-risk internal assistants require owner approval and an offline quality score of at least 80 percent on their designated benchmark before release.
A dedicated red-team review is recommended but is not mandatory for every standard-risk iteration.

Atlas Annual Subscription Terms
Annual prepaid subscriptions may be cancelled within 30 calendar days of the initial purchase for a prorated refund of the unused term. Renewals can be
stopped before the renewal date, but a renewed annual term is otherwise non-refundable except where law requires. Usage-based overage charges are excluded
from the subscription refund calculation.

Atlas Monthly Subscription Terms
Monthly subscriptions can be cancelled at any time and remain active through the end of the paid month. Monthly fees already charged are not prorated or
refunded for unused days, except where required by law. There is no thirty-day annual-purchase refund rule for monthly subscriptions.
